mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% signals accommodative monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as capital costs decline.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS below 0.5% for 3 consecutive months correlates with negative S&P 500 20-day returns in >55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.2pp monthly decline in unemployment rate signals labor market tightening, accelerating corporate profit growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE decline >0.2pp in month correlates with negative S&P 500 5-day returns in >55% of events.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential sales (RSAFS) and industrial production (INDPRO) >0.1% signal broad economic contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days due to earnings deterioration.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and INDPRO both decline >0.1% in 1 month
failure_condition: RSAFS and INDPRO decline >0.1% in month correlates with positive S&P 500 60-day returns in >55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL y/y >5.0%) triggers Fed tightening expectations, increasing bond yields and reducing equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL y/y >5.0% correlates with positive S&P 500 20-day returns in >55% of periods.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) above 102.0 (2017=100) signals strong manufacturing expansion, driving positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days via earnings acceleration.
failure_condition: INDPRO >102.0 correlates with negative S&P 500 5-day returns in >55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: New housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 1,700,000 units signals robust consumer spending, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days through economic momentum.
failure_condition: HOUST >1,700,000 correlates with negative S&P 500 20-day returns in >55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate below 4.0% indicates extreme labor market tightness, fueling wage inflation and Fed rate hikes that depress S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE <4.0% correlates with positive S&P 500 60-day returns in >55% of periods.

mechanism_narrative: Positive GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates expanding economic activity, supporting positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days through sustained corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: Positive GDPC1 growth correlates with negative S&P 500 20-day returns in >55% of periods.
